prerequisites: Basic knowledge of programming languages and fundamental algorithms for managing elementary data structures

learning_outcomes.text: The student must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the issues related to the design of elementary machines, with particular reference to elementary machines for basic and arithmetic applications, and sequential machines (registers, counters, flip-flops).

The student must also demonstrate knowledge of computer architectures and their subsystems, including processor operation, communication methods with memory, memory sizing, and connection with various input and output devices.
The student must demonstrate the ability to design and develop elementary combinational networks, arithmetic combinational networks, and sequential networks.
The student must also be able to develop simple programs in assembly language for managing elementary data structures (vectors, stacks,…).

syllabus_topics: Analysis and synthesis of combinational networks
Minimization of completely and incompletely specified Boolean functions
Synthesis of combinational networks in NAND and NOR logic
Delays and hazard problems in combinational networks
Elementary arithmetic machines: adders, subtractors, comparators
Analysis and synthesis of sequential networks
Models for timing and structure of synchronous and asynchronous sequential networks
Flip-flops: generalities, RS NOR gate flip-flops
The electronic computer: subsystems and architecture
The role of the control unit
Accumulator processors and general-purpose register processors
I/O management via polling and interrupts
Correspondence between high-level languages and machine language
Assembly and execution of programs in assembly language
Parameter passing techniques to machine language procedures
teaching_methods: Practical lessons (30% combinational machines, synchronous machines, assembly language programming)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a preliminary written test which includes exercises on the analysis and design of combinational networks, sequential networks, and the development of an assembler program. The exam is structured into a written and an oral test. Written questions can be free-response and numerical exercises.
